> The content assembly line: short vertical clips cut to the beat, narrated reels, captions and hooks, and download → transcribe → script → narrate → fan-out — its own navig-pipeline command, with your own keys; also `navig pipeline` inside navig.

**Works on its own** — its own CLI, no navig required · v0.2.2 · [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/navig-pipeline/)

**On its own** (no navig needed)

```bash
pip install navig-pipeline
navig-pipeline --help   # no navig needed
```

**With navig**

```bash
pip install navig-pipeline
navig pipeline --help
```

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `navig pipeline captions` | ✍️  Transcribe a track to an .srt — with word-level timings. |
| `navig pipeline clip` | 🎵 Build a vertical clip cut to a track you already have — no narration. |
| `navig pipeline hooks` | 🎣 Rank the passages of a track worth cutting a short clip from. |
| `navig pipeline reel` | 🎬 Build a vertical reel per language — capture, narrate, caption, score. |
| `navig pipeline run` | Run the assembly line from a topic (or a source clip) to a fanned-out post. |
| `navig pipeline schedule` | Autopilot — run + publish the assembly line on a recurring cadence. |
| `navig pipeline status` | Show which assembly-line stages are wired (their plugin is installed). |
| `navig pipeline telegram-import` | Import a Telegram channel's media into the local library, then optionally delete the |

</details>

<!-- navig:plugin-card:end -->

The **content assembly line**: short vertical clips cut to the beat, narrated reels, captions
and hooks, and a download → transcribe → script → narrate → publish flow. It runs on its own
as `navig-pipeline`, and inside navig as `navig pipeline`.

```
acquire (navig-download) → transcribe (navig-audio) → script (navig-text)
     → narrate (navig-audio) → publish (navig-social)
```

## On its own

```bash
pip install navig-pipeline                     # adds the `navig-pipeline` command
navig-pipeline status                          # which stages are wired here
navig-pipeline captions track.mp3              # word-timed .srt — no key needed (local Whisper)
navig-pipeline hooks track.mp3                 # passages worth cutting, with timings
navig-pipeline clip shot.md --range 30-45      # a vertical clip cut to the beat (ffmpeg on PATH)
navig-pipeline reel episode.md                 # narrated reel from a scenario
pip install "navig-pipeline[all]"              # + the script, acquire and publish stages of `run`
navig-pipeline run --topic "…" --dry-run
```

The media engine comes from navig-generate and the voice from navig-audio, both installed with
this. Captions use navig-audio's transcription: the OpenAI Whisper API when an OpenAI key is
set, faster-whisper on this machine otherwise. Keys come from the environment or the shared
vault (`navig-vault`).

**Filming a live URL** in a clip or reel drives your installed Chrome through navig-browser
(`pip install "navig-pipeline[film]"`, also in `[all]`); generated shots and stills need no
browser. Two things are part of navig and say so when used without it: **`schedule`** (navig's
daemon runs it) and `telegram-import` (navig's Telegram client).

## Inside navig

The same commands are `navig pipeline …`, plus the Telegram and scheduling features above.

## Why it exists

Capabilities compose. The pipeline reaches across plugins through the same public seams a
user would (navig-audio's transcription and narration, navig-generate's media engine,
navig-social's fan-out), and every stage is optional: a plugin that isn't installed drops its
stage, reported rather than silently skipped. `run` is a **dry run** unless you pass `--live`.
